extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, compositors, and academic publishers (University press style users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, copyediting, and typesetting manuscripts for publication, covering capitalization, punctuation, italics, numbers, tables, spacing, hyphenation, and typographic conventions used by an academic press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: general principles and classes of words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalization of proper names, proper nouns, principal words in titles, Christian names, familiar names applied to particular persons, regions, political divisions, organizations, religious denominations, philosophical schools, movements, peoples/races/tribes, and other classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: proper names capitalized (i), proper nouns capitalization and avoidance of division (i, 5, 53, 218); principal words in titles capitalized (41) with definition of principal words (41); Christian names to be spelled out (93); familiar names applied to particular persons capitalized (21); capitalization rules for political divisions, parties, organizations, regions, states and territories, regiments, schools, religious sects, philosophical schools, movements, peoples/races/tribes, sacred books, planets (references throughout index: e.g., 5, 6-7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 29, 32, 33, 40-49). Also special cases (e.g., University of Chicago internal titles capitalized in official work, 49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and titles of works: formatting and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format and capitalize titles of books, articles, periodicals, newspapers, pamphlets, plays, poems, poems in cycles, papers (addresses), proceedings, treatises, transactions, series, tracts, sermons, toasts, works of art, legal causes and proceedings, and subdivisions of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal words in titles capitalized (41); definite article should not be treated as part of newspaper/magazine titles (43); use of italics for titles indicated for many classes (60); roman-quotation for some shorter items (74-82); when titles/subdivisions should be spelled out (92-105); titles of legal causes italicized (63); rules for titles in various languages (English, Latin, French, Italian, Spanish, Scandinavian, German, Danish, Dutch) (42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics vs. roman-quotation: when to italicize or roman-quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to use italics and when to use roman-quotation (roman-quote) for titles, subdivisions, short works, and other quoted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of italics for many classes of titles (60); roman-quote defined (74, 253) and used for certain shorter items (e.g., short poems, articles) (81-82); preface/index and some subdivisions omit quotation marks (82); letters about how to set 'To be continued' and other running text conventions (73, 179).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation: overall rules and placement with quotations/refs
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for periods, commas, semicolons, colons, interrogation and exclamation points, and other punctuation marks including their placement with quotation marks and in references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules enumerated 121-214; placing of period with quotation marks (126); rules for use of period (122-126) including omissions after headlines and certain abbreviations (125, 123, 124); semicolon usage in enumerations and separation of distinct clauses, placement with quotation marks (137-140); use of colon with 'namely' and placing with quotation marks (132, 136); interrogation and exclamation point rules (129-130, 128); use and omission of commas in series and sequences (143); rules for punctuation in classical references and Scripture (237, 239, 134).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks and quotation handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use double vs single quotation marks; when quotation marks should be omitted; punctuation in relation to quotation marks; special rules for reduced citations and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks not to be used in reduced citations (87) with exceptions (75); placing of colon, comma, ellipsis, exclamation point, interrogation point, and period in connection with quotation marks (136, 162, 181, 128, 130, 126); use of double and single quotation marks (91); omit quotation marks in references to Preface, Index, etc. (82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations: formatting, capitalization of first word, and when to run in or reduce
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set block and run-in quotations, reduction rules, and capitalization of the first word depending on connection to surrounding text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations treatment rules 74-91; first word of a quotation lower-cased when connected with the previous sentence (57); when to reduce quotations, when to run them into text (85); use of indention and paragraph marks (85, 274).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals: spelling, figures, punctuation, and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to spell out numbers versus set in figures, treatment of consecutive numbers, groups, round numbers, use of commas for thousands, use of dash for ranges, and spacing of numerals in lines/headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers commencing a sentence to be spelled out (96); connected groups to be treated alike (94); groups of six or more closely connected to be set in figures (94); numbers of less than three digits spelled out in ordinary reading matter (94); round numbers treatment (95); use of comma after digits indicating thousands (159); use of comma to separate numbers (154); dash as 'to' connecting numbers (173); Arabic and Roman numerals spacing at beginning of lines and headlines (271); omission of period after numerals (124).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates, time, money, units, percentages: formatting and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format dates and times, sums of money, units of measurement, percentage expression and unit symbols and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date rules including omission of s, d, th in dates (102); time of day, how to treat (98) and punctuation of indications (134); sums of money how to treat (97) and spacing of monetary symbols (270); units of measurement abbreviations and spelling with lowercase initial (55); per cent to be expressed in figures and not treated as an abbreviation (94, 123); spacing rules for metric symbols and designation of metric weights and measures (269, in).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and omission: periods and indication of omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use and omission of periods after abbreviations (including MS, initials, epoch abbreviations), and marking omitted letters or words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of period after initials of titles of publications (123); omission of period after Roman numerals (124); omission of period after headlines etc. (125); omission of s, d, th in dates (102); use of apostrophe to indicate omitted letters/figures (163); 'Op. cit.' usage (233); lists of literary abbreviations (no) and states/Old/New Testament abbreviations (109, 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and compounds: prefixes, suffixes, and compounding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on hyphenation and treatment of compounds with prefixes and suffixes (including co-, re-, pre-, sub-, semi-, quasi-, tri-, super-, ultra-, un-, under-, post-, 'self', 'mother', 'father', 'shop', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefix or suffix not complete in itself to be indicated by hyphen (212); rules for compounds with 'co-','pre-','re-','sub-','semi-','quasi-','tri-','super-','ultra-','un-','under-','post-','pre-','re-','sub-','semi-' with specific index entries 197-209, 186-209; list of hyphenated words (214); two-letter syllables avoidance in divisions (216); treatment of 'short and' (104, 107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing and spaces in composition and typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for spacing in foundry, linotype, and monotype composition; sizes of spaces; thin and thick spaces; where to avoid wide or thin spacing; spacing of punctuation, figures in tables, and mathematical formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for spacing 258-73; spacing in foundry type and general composition explained (261-64); linotype spacing (260); monotype spacing (259); specimens and different sizes of spaces (261); what is considered good standard spacing (262); thin-spacing where to avoid (265); spacing of divisional signs, figure columns in tables, formulae, headlines, metric and monetary symbols, numerals at beginning of paragraphs, Scripture passages, short words (various refs: 269-273, 245, 273, 271, 272, 268).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work: design, open vs ruled tables, headlines, and typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting tables: two-column open tables, tables of more than two columns as ruled, box-heads, headlines for open tables, reading-matter in columns, specimen tables, rules for use of rules in tables and use of small caps in tabular work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for setting tables 241-50; two-column tables to be set as open (248); tables of more than two as ruled (248); open tables headlines for columns (242); box-heads for ruled tables (242); reading-matter in columns of ruled tables how to set (246); use of small caps in tabular work (242, 249); specimen tables (250); rules for use of rules in tables (243, 247).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic styles, sizes, and type terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and examples of type styles (roman, italic, small caps), sizes (pica, minion, small pica), special units (quad, ems), point system, and names of many specific typefaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Styles of type discussed 253-57; small caps defined and indicated (257) and their use in headings and tables (52, 279, 242, 249); pica, minion, small pica explained (252); point system explanation (251-52); three-em/ two-em dashes and quads defined and illustrated (261); specimens of types listed and shown (pages with specimen types and sample text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and proofreading: definitions, marks, hints, and page/plate-proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of page-proof, plate-proof, proofs and revise; guidance and hints for proofreaders and the marks to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page-proof defined (286); plate-proof defined (287); proofs description 285-89; 'revise' defined (289); hints to proofreaders and marks for proofreaders (pp. 117-19; p. 123).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and reference indices: marks and sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of section mark, paragraph mark, parallel mark, superior figures as reference indices; rules for sequences of footnote indices and subdivisional numberings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section mark spacing and use for footnote index (269, 232); paragraph mark spacing and use for footnote index (269, 232); parallel mark for footnote index (232); superior figures used for reference indices (232, 234); sequences of footnote indices and subdivisional numbering rules (232, 176).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and parenthetical clauses: punctuation and nesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of parentheses, use in connection with figures/letters indicating subsections, placing of period, use of brackets within parentheses, and punctuation for parenthetical clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for parentheses 176-77; use of parentheses for parenthetical clauses (177) with cross-refs to commas and dashes (150, 167); use of brackets within parentheses (178); placing of period in connection with parentheses (126); use of commas/dashes with parenthetical clauses (150, 167, 169).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings, running heads, side-heads, and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set and punctuate side-heads, running-heads, and headings; omission of periods; use of dashes; capitalization conventions; and rules for signatures at end of letters or articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running-heads defined with omission of period after (125, 283) and hints for setting (283); side-heads defined with omission of period after, use of dash, and use of lower case (56, 172, 125, 280); omission of period after side-heads and running-heads (125); use of dash in connection with side-heads (172); omission of comma and period after signatures and setting rules for signatures (161, 125, 50, 65).

rubrics_metrics.name: References, citations, and legal/literary reference formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for formatting literary and legal references, abbreviations used, punctuation in references, use of dash in references, and treatment of subdivisions in literary references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal references: list of words/phrases used in legal refs (61); literary references: list of words to be abbreviated and punctuation rules (no, 237, 239); use of dash in connection with references (174); subdivisions in literary references use lower case (54) and letters indicating subdivisions to be set in italics (66); 'Vol., chap., p.' treatment with numerals and omission rules (237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific, biological, paleontological, and zoological names: capitals and italics
rubrics_metrics.description: When to capitalize scientific and zoological names and when to set them in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific terms: use of capitals in certain contexts (46) and of italics (71); species and scientific names: capitalization and italics rules (46, 71); paleontological terms caps and italics guidance (46, 71); zoological terms capitalization and italics (46, 71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language- and name-specific rules: particles, prefixes, and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat name particles (van, von, de, van der, 'Mac', 'O', umlauted names), indexing rules for initials and special characters, and treatment of foreign place-names and translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particles in French, Dutch, and German names capitalization (3); rules for 'van' and 'von' treatment and indexing (3, 240); 'Mac','Me','M'' treatment (240); indexing of 'St.' and umlaut initial names (240); translation of names of foreign institutions and foreign words/phrases (11, 59, 78); place-names foreign treatment (59).
